pageCache.pageTitle: Warfield CE Primary School - Modern Foreign Languages
pageCache.text:
Modern Foreign Languages
"Knowledge of languages is the doorway to wisdom."
Roger Bacon (English Philosopher)
Languages at Warfield
Within our school community over 27 different languages are spoken. We value all languages and encourage children to share their home language with us.
From Year 3 through to Year 6, we then begin to learn French.
We believe that learning a language is a life-long, cultural and linguistic skill, especially in an increasingly globalised world. Learning a modern foreign language enables the children to develop new skills and confidence; it promotes initiative and broadens their understanding of the world and diversity within society.
How we deliver our curriculum
At Warfield School, we follow a scheme from Language Angels with purposefully designed progressive French lessons, whereby our children develop the ability to read, write and converse in French. Our teaching exposes children to the written and spoken language through a range of songs and stories, which enhances the learning of vocabulary and grammar. In addition to the language, children are taught about traditions in French speaking countries.
We are supported by a French teacher, who delivers lunchtime French clubs to both KS1 and KS2; this allows children to opportunity to develop their skills further if they wish.
How we support everyone to learn
The learning of French incorporates all learners, irrespective of their ability and needs. In fact the learning of a language can often challenge preconceived ideas about ability.
Our teaching is very interactive using a range of strategies to aid visual and auditoria experiences, including pictures, songs and stories. These practical approaches help children to make links between pictures, the sound the word makes and what it looks like written down.
We support those who are already fluent through working with families and wider agencies to provide challenging learning opportunities.
On rare occasions a child's need in the English language might be so significant that introducing a new language could be to the detriment of their learning, discussion between the school and parents will determine how best to support the child if this is the case.

pageCache.pageTitle: Warfield CE Primary School - Maths at Warfield
pageCache.text:
Maths
"Mathematics is the most beautiful and most powerful creation of the human spirit." - Stefan Banach (Polish mathematician)
We strive to impart a well-rounded mathematical proficiency in students - one that goes beyond rote learning to enable application and transfer of skills to real world contexts. Our mathematics curriculum aims to develop conceptual fluency, adaptive reasoning, creative problem solving, precise communicating, and curious questioning.
The rationale is that mathematics is more than formulas and mechanics - it is a lens to make sense of reality, a tool to tackle daily challenges, and a language to express abstract ideas that uplift human thought and progress. Students equipped with mathematical empowerment can think more logically, question more intelligently, reason more systematically, and contribute more inventively.
Our commitment is to inspire students' mathematical confidence and competence so they are primed for excellence in the future.
How we deliver our curriculum
Children from Reception to Year 6 follow The White Rose programme: a programme to meet the criteria for high-quality teaching of mastery in England. This is complimented with other resources such as Third Space Learning.
All of our resources follow an exciting growth mind set and problem-solving approach. All children are encouraged to believe in their ability to master maths and are empowered to succeed through curiosity and persistence, while tackling the same concepts at the same time and progressing together as a whole class. The 'small step approach' allows children to keep up not catch up.
Also, within each unit that is covered, the 'concrete - pictorial - abstract' approach to mastery maths is used.
The use of manipulatives allows children to have a tangible link to their learning.
The use of pictorial representations enables children to understand how the focus maths skills can be represented in a number of different ways - mastering the small steps to learning and ensuring the learning is not just 'discrete'.
From this process, children are then able to approach the maths in a more abstract manner but, by using their previous knowledge and skills, can apply the small steps to understanding and solving the problem.
How we support everyone to learn
We believe all children are capable of achieving to a high standard and therefore never put glass ceilings upon their learning. We understand that high-quality teaching practice is the best proven method for supporting all children to succeed.
Teachers will use resources tailored to individuals needs to support them in their learning so that they are able to achieve the same outcomes as all. Additionally, many concepts in maths are taught alongside the use of manipulatives (concrete resources) which allows children to be hands-on and to 'see' the maths that they are learning.

Science
"The important thing is to never stop questioning."
Albert Einstein (German physicist)
Within our school, science learning is driven by exploring, enquiring and explaining. We believe the in importance in cultivating a sense of excitement about the world around us and a curiosity to understanding it further.
Through a hands-on, inquiry-based curriculum, children will experience the joy of exploration and investigation. We foster enthusiasm and creativity through themed science weeks to ensure all children have the opportunity to explore a theme in greater depth.
How we deliver our curriculum
At Warfield School, we have carefully designed our curriculum to ensure a progression of skills and knowledge in line with the National Curriculum.
All year groups teach an explicit science-based topic for 3 half-terms, driven by a 'Big Question', which seeks to link different lessons within a topic together. Children learn through small-steps, building on previous learning to be able to answer the 'Big Question' at the end of the topic. 'Big Question' responses are not always written, essay-style answers, allowing children to demonstrate their knowledge, creativity and passion when answering.
Our Science learning links closely to cross-curricular activities, such as practical applications of Computing and Maths. Throughout the school, children are encouraged to collect, record, present and analyse data in different ways, such as using graphs or tables. We encourage children's historical thinking, when investigating the inventions and achievements of scientists over time.
How we support everyone to learn
Science learning incorporates all learners, irrespective of their ability and needs.
Our teaching is investigation-led and highly interactive. Practical resources and materials are frequently used to physically model new learning. Children are then given opportunities to investigate the concept themselves, working independently, in partners or within small groups.
All classrooms display their currently topic, full of key vocabulary and diagrams to support learning. Lessons use pictures and Widgit images, and adults model accurate use of new scientific vocabulary. These practical approaches help children to make links between their learning and have an anchor to refer back to in future lessons. Teaching and learning styles are differentiated to provide appropriate challenge and scaffold to all learners.

Computing
Technology opens the door to the world. It's up to us to walk through it in a meaningful and respectful way.
Dr. Daniel L Frazier
Computing at Warfield
Computational thinking is vital to make sense of the world and it's systems, both man-made and natural. It has the power to change lives and rewrite the future. From travelling across space to communicating with friends, computing is at the core of our world. Thinking logically, planning sequentially and finding elusive bugs in the system are all essential skills honed when refining programmes to solve real world problems. As citizens of the online community, children here at Warfield need to act responsibly; the digital world is vast and needs to be navigated safely.
How we deliver our curriculum
At Warfield Primary School, we have designed a Computing curriculum which is ambitious, engaging and accessible in order for all learners to succeed.
Computing is an integral part of the school curriculum due to its links within modern society and how these technologies are used within everyday life. Our computing curriculum caters for this by ensuring children’s learning focuses on creating, designing and communicating as well as problem solving.
Our computing curriculum follows the National Curriculum and is organised into 3 main strands.
At the heart of our curriculum is understanding big computational ideas (such as sequence, selection and iteration), then through practice, using these to solve problems, write programmes and design content.
Equally important are using information technology and digital literacy; the ability to express ideas creatively, using the best program for the task, is a life skill we start embedding through the digital literacy strand of our curriculum. The final strand of our curriculum is equipping children to be safe and discerning digital citizens who know how to interact safely in their ever-expanding virtual world.
When children leave our school, we aim for them to be Digital Creators, Communicators and Citizens. They will have a broad set of skills to support and enhance their learning, therefore providing them with life skills in preparation for an ever growing digital world.
How we support everyone to learn
To support the diverse needs of all learners we ensure our Computing lessons are appropriately adapted to engage and be inclusive for all. We have access to a range of equipment (e.g. specialist larger keyboards, dictation devices, ipads) which are accessible to children with additional needs. Children are able to broaden and deepen their knowledge of this subject by joining in with lunchtime and after school clubs.

PSHCE & RSE
Educating the mind without educating the heart is no education at all
PSHCE is an integral part of teaching within Warfield CE School. We value and promote children’s personal, social and economic development as well as their health and well being. Within our teaching we give children the knowledge, skills and understanding they need to lead confident, healthy, independent lives and to become informed and kind citizens.
We follow the KAPOW Scheme which is adapted for our children to ensure there is clear progression throughout the school. Teachers plan and teach, based on the needs and interests of their children in their class and adapt lessons in order to both support and challenge learning and understanding.
Children are encouraged to be individuals and develop good relationships with their peers and staff to take responsibility for their own behaviour. All staff provide good role models for children and work hard to promote a safe and happy environment.
How we deliver our curriculum
At Warfield School, we follow a scheme from KAPOW with purposefully designed progressive PSHCE lessons. PSHCE is taught under five headings. These are the same for each year group for Years 1 to 6.: Families & Relationships, Safety & the Changing Body, Health & Well being, Citizenship and Economic Wellbeing.
The Early Years Curriculum covers PSHCE through the strand of Personal Social and Emotional Development (PSED). PSED is not taught in isolation rather it is an ongoing strand throughout a child's time within Early Years.
A key aspect of delivering good quality PSHCE involves quality circle time. Quality Circle Time is a democratic approach used by teachers to manage issues that effect the whole class. it ahs been proved to promote better relationships and also helps with positive behaviour management.
How we support everyone to learn
The learning of PSHCE is taught every week and is a core subject. PSHCE incorporates every learner, regardless of their ability and needs. In fact the learning of PSHCE is so varied and can often highlight preconceived ideas which can .be openly discussed in a safe environment.
Teachers plan using KAPOW and will often enhance the learning opportunities through visuals and key questions to promote extended thinking to ensure it is all inclusive.
Our teaching of PSHCE involves and offers active participation as well as the opportunity to record in written form. This could be either in a child's individual PSHCE book in pictures/ photos or written form in a class floor book.

pageCache.pageTitle: Warfield CE Primary School - Early Years
pageCache.text:
Early Years
"Children learn as they play; most importantly, in play, children learn how to learn."
Early Years at Warfield
At the heart of our Early Years is our children. We aim to spark curiosity and grow a love of learning from the very start. Through a culture of kindness, respect, and teamwork, children learn to value themselves and others around them. Our approach is rooted in learning through play, play is how young children explore, discover, and make sense of the world around them in a safe and stimulating way. We encourage children to challenge themselves and feel proud of their achievements. Through our curriculum, we are able to provide children with rich and diverse experiences for them to investigate their world, this may be through activities such as story telling, creating pieces of art, role play, or experiments. We celebrate each child’s journey of achievement, promoting determination and resilience as they grow.
In the classroom, we use a variety of learning styles suited to the Early Years, free-flow, small group discussions, whole class lessons. Our children are able to develop relationships, grow their self-awareness and improve their communication and language skills by taking part in role paly in our Home Corner or building in our Construction Area or exploring their art and design ideas in our Creative Area.
The children have daily access to a well-resourced outdoor area during our free-flow time. This provides them with a variety of learning opportunities such as construction, water and sand play and performing on their very own stage. The children also have access to our meadow space which is a beautiful natural environment for them to explore and use their imagination in. It has a range of outdoor equipment for children to use and develop their gross motor skills. By learning and playing outside, the children find out about the natural environment, how to manage risks and how to use their own initiative to solve problems and co-operate with others. Through various activities and play children learn boundaries of behaviour; both physical and social, grow in self-confidence and become self-motivated.
Our aim is for children to leave our Early Years settings with a firm foundation to build upon not only in their learning but all areas of their development.
How we support everyone to learn
In Early Years we provide individualised support for children in a variety of ways. We provide small group learning with a specific focus which will develop the skills the children need to gain more effective access to the Early Years curriculum and become successful and independent. We provide a range of resources to ensure all children are able to join in with their school day confidently, such as, visuals, concrete number resources and sensory supports. Children who join our Early Years who have identified needs already are supported though a range of transition activities and on going communication and support from specialist outside agencies.

English
"Reading is to the mind what exercise is to the body" - Joseph Addison
"Start writing, no matter what. The water does not flow until the faucet is turned on" - Louis L'Amour
At Warfield, we aim to equip children with the essential language skills to speak, read and write confidently with enjoyment, helping them build valuable life skills and cultural awareness. We build on the language children bring from home by offering rich and varied linguistic experiences. English is a key skill that underpins learning across all subjects, enabling pupils to access the full curriculum and express themselves effectively in any context. Our goal is for all pupils to become fluent readers, articulate speakers, active listeners and confident writers. They will develop strong vocabulary, grammar, comprehension skills, learn to express opinions, emotions and responses to a range of texts. Pupils will write clearly and effectively, adapting style to suit different purposes and audiences and will plan, draft and edit to improve their work. Further to this, at Warfield, we foster a love of literature, encourage discussion as a tool for learning and integrate high-quality literacy experiences across the curriculum.
How we deliver our curriculum:
Being able to read is the most important skill children will learn during their early schooling. It is our vision that through our purposeful approach to teaching Early Reading & Phonics, every child will be able to read confidently, fluently and accurately with understanding and enjoyment by the end of their primary schooling; all central to developing understanding across our broad and balanced curriculum. At Warfield, we use Essential Letters and Sounds. This enables children at Warfield to deploy a full range of reading cues - phonic, graphic, syntactic, contextual, and to monitor, correct and make sense of their own reading as they deepen their skill sets. By doing so, children grow and move from ‘learning to read’ to ‘reading to learn’ for purpose and pleasure enabling children to access evermore challenging texts into and throughout KS2. We foster enthusiasm in words and their meanings for comprehension and to gain an appreciation and love of books from a variety of genres and media (fiction, non-fiction, poetry, reading scheme books, ‘real’ books, e-books etc).
Warfield uses Essential Letters and Sounds, a synthetic phonics programme, backed by Oxford University Press. It teaches children how sounds are presented by written letters. Children are taught to read words by blending these sounds together to make words. For example, they will be taught that the letters ‘m-a-t’ blend together to make ‘mat’. A synthetic phonics programme, such as ELS, is a structure for teaching these sounds in a certain order to build up children’s learning gradually. It is used daily during Reception and Year 1 to teach all the sounds in the English language.
With ELS, there is a daily phonics lesson where the teacher teaches a new sound, or reviews sounds learned earlier in the week. This is shown to the class on the whiteboard.
Children learn the letters that represent the sounds. They are then asked to read words and sentences with the new sounds in. Children will also practise writing the letters that represent the sounds.
What order are the sounds taught in?
New sounds are taught each day, with some review days and weeks to help children practise what they’ve learned.
Click below to reveal the sounds your child will learn in ELS:
Phase 2 Phase 3 Phase 5
How should the sounds be pronounced?
Children learn to read letters or groups of letters by saying the sounds they represent. Pronounce the sounds as you would say them within a word. Make sure you don’t add ‘uh’ onto the end, so for ‘m’ say ‘mm’ not ‘muh’ and for ‘l’ say ‘ull’ not ‘luh’.
Click below to show you how to pronounce the sounds:
Phase 2Phase 3 Phase 5
How can I help at home?
We want children to create a strong orthographic map. This means that they learn sounds spelt by the letters or groups of letters in each word. This is especially important when ‘alternatives’ in the English language appear.
To read fluently, or well, we need a strong orthographic map.
To consistently recognise that the ea in bread spells /e/ we need to read it at least 4 times. This means we need to read the word many times to build fluency for reading. This is why we advocate for not changing a book straight away.
Practising the Sounds:
Through our writing curriculum, it is our vision that every child will become a creative writer by being given exciting, inspiring and engaging materials and opportunities that challenge and support them. We want children to become confident, talented, enthusiastic writers who develop a love for writing. They will be able to use writing to communicate with others and express themselves and be able to write independently for a range of purposes. Children will be able to reflect upon and evaluate their writing, use vocabulary to create style and convey meaning and use what they read to enhance what they write. As they progress, children will deepen their knowledge of meaning and purpose within their writing. At Warfield, we have designed a curriculum that incorporates a variety of techniques to support children in their writing development, with a focus on Talk for Writing. Teachers plan and teach based on the needs and interests of their class and adapt lessons in order to support and challenge learning. We regularly assess independent pieces of writing across classes and year groups to identify gaps, inform planning and monitor progress.

History
"Study the past if you want to define the future."
Confucius (Chinese Philosopher)
At Warfield School, we aim to understand the significance of historical events and how they have shaped our present day. We aim to bring alive the past by making our History learning engaging and inspiring, whilst exploring various cultures and societies. Through the teaching of History, children will be equipped with the skills to ask perceptive questions, think critically, weigh evidence, sift arguments, and develop perspective and judgement, which will help them develop a sense of identity and understand the complexity of people's lives.
How we deliver our curriculum
Our curriculum has been carefully designed to allow for skills to progress as the children move through the school. We teach children a sense of chronology, and through this they develop a cultural understanding based on their historical heritage. Successively they learn to value their own and other people’s cultures in modern multicultural Britain by stimulating the children’s interest and understanding about the life of people; how they thought and relate it to today's world view. By considering how people lived in the past, they are better able to make their own life choices today.
Our History aims to inspire in pupils a curiosity and fascination about the world and its people which links readily to cross curricular links in all other areas. For example, many topics link well with the creative arts, which allows children to explore different mediums.
In our school, History makes a significant contribution to citizenship education by teaching about how Britain developed as a democratic society. We teach children to understand how events in the past have influenced our lives today; we also teach them to investigate these past events and by doing so, to develop the skills of enquiry, analysis, interpretation and problem solving.
How we support everyone to learn
The learning of History incorporates all learners, irrespective of their ability and needs. We plan differentiation in our History; providing a variety of teaching and learning styles and differentiated opportunities, appropriate to all ability levels.
In History we use a diverse range of materials to engage and maximise our pupils' talents; artefacts, art, eye-witness accounts, fiction and photography. By using a range of visual sources, children can explore through discussions what they can learn and infer about specific time periods. Where responses are written, appropriate scaffolds are in place to support learners expressing their opinions or alternative methods (like voice/ video recording) can be used to record thoughts.
Across all year groups , in–house and external History experiences compliment, embed, extend and enhance the children’s confidence and interest in history.​

Physical Education
“Sport has literally changed my life. I’m here because of sport. It has given me a lot of confidence, a lot of courage, and a lot of discipline. It’s helped me to be the person that I’ve grown to be today.”
Serena Williams (Tennis Player)
At Warfield, we believe that physical education should take place in a safe and supportive environment. We recognise that PE is a unique and vital contributor to pupils’ physical development and well-being. Our broad and balanced PE curriculum is designed to build pupils’ self-confidence as they learn to manage themselves and their bodies in a variety of movement situations. Progressive learning objectives, combined with thoughtful and varied teaching approaches, aim to provide stimulating, enjoyable, satisfying, and appropriately challenging learning experiences for all pupils.
We are fortunate at Warfield to have the support of two specialist PE coaches who assist teachers during PE sessions and support children at the many sporting events offered by Bracknell Forest. As a result of this additional adult support, we are able to offer a range of extra-curricular clubs for all age groups throughout the year.
How we deliver our curriculum
We are committed to delivering a high-quality, inclusive PE curriculum that inspires all pupils to succeed and enjoy being active. We use the Complete PE scheme to provide structured, progressive lessons that develop physical skills, teamwork, and a lifelong love of sport and physical activity. To further strengthen our provision, we are supported by two qualified sports coaches who work alongside class teachers to deliver high-impact lessons. This collaborative approach not only enhances the quality of PE teaching but also builds staff confidence and ensures consistency across the school. Together, we aim to provide every child with positive, meaningful PE experiences that support their physical and emotional well-being.
How we support everyone to learn
We believe that all children can benefit from Physical Education and should have equal access to opportunities that develop their physical, social, and emotional skills. Our inclusive approach to PE is rooted in the belief that every child can succeed and feel valued, regardless of ability or background. We are committed to creating a safe, supportive, and motivating environment where all students are encouraged to participate and thrive. To remove barriers to participation, we adapt activities and instruction to meet individual needs—this includes modifying rules, offering varying levels of challenge, using assistive technologies, and providing personalised support. Our teachers and qualified sports coaches use a variety of teaching styles, grouping strategies, and accessible resources to ensure lessons are inclusive, engaging, and enjoyable. Staff are trained to identify and support pupils with additional needs and continue to receive professional development to enhance their practice. We also work closely with families to identify and overcome any challenges to participation, and we celebrate the achievements of all pupils to promote confidence and a love of physical activity.

Geography
"Geography is the tapestry that weaves the world together" -
Gil Grosvenor (Former President of National Geographic)
Geography at Warfield
Our geography curriculum aims to instill a sense of awe and wonder about the world around us. As the children begin their Warfield journey, we encourage them to develop a sense of curiosity and fascination so that they can think for themselves, to take initiative, to ask questions and investigate our world.
Within our school community, we have many families with connections to other countries so we encourage children to share their knowledge. This helps to enrich their social, moral, and cultural development. We are committed to developing ‘Geographers for Life’ and instilling them with investigative and problem-solving skills for use both inside the classroom and beyond. With these skills we hope to develop our children into educated citizens who can make a valuable change to our world.
How we deliver our curriculum
At Warfield School, we use a variety of multi-media resources including ICT to engage our children and allow them to independently select and research a broader range of geographical information.
Based upon the Early Years Foundation Stage Statutory Framework 2021, Geography is integrated within The world around us as well as continuous provision throughout the year during freeflow. In years 1-6, Geography (physical and human) is taught both as discrete topics and within other subject areas such as History. The curriculum is mapped out to ensure that knowledge and skills are both revised and built upon from Year 1 up to Year 6. The curriculum is enriched with trips out of school and fieldwork within the school environment. Throughout the topic, the children explore and investigate Geographical themes to answer an enquiry question. Helping them to showcase and relate their learning to wider world.
How we support everyone to learn
The learning of Geography incorporates all learners, irrespective of their ability and needs. We provide a broad, balanced and diverse geography curriculum that both supports and challenges all children to ensure progression.
Our teaching is very interactive using a range of strategies to aid visual and auditorial experiences, including pictures, songs and stories. In addition, we use consistent technical vocabulary, displays to support understanding of challenging concepts and practical opportunities to reinforce knowledge. These practical approaches help children to make links between the pictures and the world around them. Knowledge is supported through scaffolding, teamwork, discussions and debates.

Extra Curricular Clubs, Trips & Experiences
Learning is more that classroom teaching, learning is enriched and enhanced through experience and opportunity to apply our knowledge in real life.
At Warfield we enrich our school life through a range of extra curricular clubs, visitors, trips and experiences.
Extra Curricular Clubs
School staff run after school and lunchtime clubs on a voluntary basis. The clubs cover a wide range of different themes, sporting, arts and craft, cooking, discussion, science, reading, gardening and each club runs for half a term. These clubs have no charge.
Sometimes external providers offer other opportunities for example music lessons, these do incur a charge and information regarding this can be obtained from the school office.
Club booking takes place via Operoo
Summer Term Clubs Timetable
Trips and Experiences
We recognise that nothing is a substitute for real life hands on experiences that are provided through visitors into and trips outside of school.
These opportunities usually have a cost in order for them to go ahead. Whilst the school works hard to minimise costs, voluntary contributions from families are essential in order to ensure these opportunities can go ahead.
During the Meet the Teacher meetings at the beginning of September you will receive an overview of approximate costs and experiences expected over the school year.
For residential trips payment schedules are implemented several months in advance of the trip.
All communications regarding trips and visits will be via Operoo. Emails and forms will be provided to authorise your child’s attendance.
Pupil Premium, Free School Meals and Trips.
The pupil premium grant is government funding that is allocated to schools in order to support the learning of disadvantaged children. The amount of funding the school gets is based on the number of children they have that fall into a number of identified vulnerable groups. For more information about pupil premium please visit this page.
The school reserves a small portion of this funding to support families whose children would otherwise would not be able to access trips and experiences.
At Warfield we strive to ensure all children are able to access these opportunities, and ask any families who are unable to support the voluntary contribution to contact the school and ask to speak to Karen Callard who will be able to help you. Please note we maintain the utmost discretion in these matters. before refusing permission for the trip.
Medications and Additional Needs
Please complete the Operoo form prior to the trip with any needs your child may have. Qualified first aiders will be able to administer minor first aid and medications with the appropriate consent.
Early in the Autumn Term you will receive an offsite permissions form which gives general permission for certain activities to occur without prior parental consent over the year, these include going for walks in the local area around school and going on the school minibus.

pageCache.pageTitle: Warfield CE Primary School - Creative Arts
pageCache.text:
Creative Arts
“You can’t use up creativity. The more you use, the more you have."
Creative Arts at Warfield
At Warfield, we believe the Creative Arts – encompassing Music, Art and Design Technology – are vital to nurturing imagination, self-expression and a deep appreciation of the world. Our curriculum offers rich, high-quality learning experiences that inspire children to explore, create and communicate through a range of artistic disciplines. The Creative Arts at Warfield encourage pupils to express their ideas and emotions through a variety of medias. They are given opportunities to experiment with materials, develop techniques, and appreciate the work of artists, promoting critical thinking and personal reflection. Design and Technology at Warfield challenges children to think practically and creatively, as they design, make and evaluate purposeful products. Through a progressive skills framework, pupils gain hands-on experience and learn to solve real-world problems, considering the needs and values of others. Across all three subjects, we provide children with a wide range of experiences that develop cultural understanding, confidence and resilience, empowering every child to find their voice and flourish through the arts.
How we deliver our curriculum
Children at Warfield learn through carefully thought-out topics that frame their learning throughout the year. Their learning in the Creative Arts is directly linked to these topics, ensuring all children are given meaningful opportunities to create with purpose and bring their learning to life. In Music, specialist teachers from Berkshire Maestros deliver engaging lessons that celebrate cultural diversity and ensure that children are equipped with the knowledge and skills they need to progress. We use Out of the Ark as a way to bring collaborative performance and the joy of singing into daily life and worship at Warfield.
How we support everyone to learn
At Warfield, we are committed to ensuring that the Creative Arts are accessible and inclusive for all children, regardless of ability or background. We recognise and celebrate the diverse needs of our learners by providing a range of strategies, adaptations and resources to support full participation. In Music, this includes using symbols, large print, gesture, and expressive voice, as well as a strong focus on aural memory. Children with additional needs are supported with accessible instruments, and those with a particular passion or talent are encouraged to develop further through opportunities with Maestros and visiting music professionals. In Art and DT, we use a wide variety of resources to enable access, such as specialist tools, visual scaffolds and sloped desks. Our approach is underpinned by high-quality planning and inclusive teaching that allows every child to take pride in their achievements. Through thoughtful adaptations and a focus on equity, we aim to ensure every child experiences success, enjoyment, and a sense of belonging in the Creative Arts.

Personal Development - What is in our backpacks? How do we belong?
At Warfield Church of England Primary School, we recognise that a child's primary school experience is a crucial time for children to develop their identity, aspirations, and understanding of the world. Our vision and values is at the heart of everything we collectively work towards for our pupils. Within our vision, we believe everyone is on a journey and we expect every child at Warfield to fill their 'backpacks' with the spritual, moral, social and cultural understanding to achieve. We believe that this personal development is crucial for every child, not just during their time at Warfield but for their future. Therefore, our values and the enrichment we offer as part of our personal development offer and which contribute to a child's backpack for the future are not just taught, they are a lived experience that every member pupil and member of staff experiences and demonstrates in their every day life. This ethos, high standards and lived experience for our pupils is recognised in our recent SIAMS inspection.
Alongside academic achievement, we place a strong emphasis on Spiritual, Moral, Social, and Cultural (SMSC) development, ensuring that every child has rich and varied experiences both within and beyond the curriculum.
By nurturing personal development skills, we equip our pupils with the essential knowledge they need to become educated citizens, preparing them for life beyond Warfield and teaching them how to engage meaningfully with society.
Throughout their time at Warfield, children are encouraged to:
By embedding these principles in all aspects of school life, we aim to nurture confident, compassionate, and well-rounded individuals who are fully prepared for the opportunities and challenges of the future.
PSHE Curriculum
Our PSHE curriculum enables us to provide children with the additional elements they need to fill their 'backpacks'. We explore the wider world with our children at the heart of everything we do. Our comprehensive curriculum explores ideas which will affect our children as they grow and develop, including challenging stereotypes including gender, age and disability as well as supporting our children to be curious and respectful. We support our children in understanding the importance of our British Values, we encourage them to be curious about the world we live in as well as understand how these values enable them to be successful in the future. Please clink the link on the right of the page to explore this in more detail.
Enrichment Activities
We recognise that the learning within our curriculum is a small part of our wider school offer. We ensure every child is given extra curricular learning opportunities throughout their time with us at Warfield. This provides them with the experiences they need to add to their 'backpacks' and gives them skills they can use throughout their lives.
On top of our external offer, all of our teachers run after school clubs these have included Lego, Stop Motion, Computing, Cooking, Construction, Netball, Football, Basketball, Choir and Gymnastics. This allows every child the opportunity to experience something new.
We also support the learning in the classroom with enrichment activities, listed below, which include local walks, residential trips as well as visits to our school from people within our community. We also provide children with the opportunity to learn from people who have different careers within STEM such as vets as well as careers within the emergency services.
Oasis
We work in conjunction with Warfield Church to provide our children with opportunities to develop their ability to create space in their busy lives for peace, reflection and consider their mental well-being. Our children all participated in a workshop, run by volunteers from Warfield Church, which focussed on opportunities for reflection. Due to the overwhelming success of this event, we have now included this in our weekly offer to our children. The children continue to benefit from this enrichment experience.
Work with our community
We are constantly developing links with our community. We are very lucky to be surrounded by a supportive and nurturing environment. Our links with the community play a huge part of our enrichment opportunities however more explicit examples include within our Harvest celebrations we work with Warfield Church to reflect and give thanks for the food we have. We also collaborate with Bracknell Foodbank to collect food and give back to those living within our community.
Our choir have participated in the Reading Music Festival for several years, performing at the Hexagon. They have also visited Brownlow Hall, to perform at Christmas for the local residents. Most recently, this was supported by the children in our Dance club too.
Leadership Opportunities
As part of our belief that children should play a part in shaping their school they are a part of as well as the world they live in. We have a school council which provides the children the opportunity to participate in and understand the idea of democracy. The school council have completed significant work around the idea of looking after our environment. They arranged for each class to be a part of a wider school promise to plant more trees on our school site. As a direct result of their work, we have attended several climate conferences as well as arranged for a local car company to deliver a clean air workshop. We are proud of our children's understanding that they are a part of the world they live in and play a huge role in shaping the future of our planet.
We also have House Team captains which represent the four houses. These are children who epitomize our school values and act as aspirational role models for younger children. This is also the case for our Sports Leaders who are chosen for their ongoing dedication to team work, athleticism and overall sporting attitude.
Our Year 5 children also take on the role of buddies, helping our children in Reception to settle in and support them throughout their first year at Warfield. Through this system, the Year 5 children support the Reception children in understanding how to play together, complete reading activities and share good learning practice.

Religious Education
"Compassion is the key in Islam and Buddhism and Judaism and Christianity. They are profoundly similar."
Karen Armstrong (English Author)
Religious Education at Warfield
Through our R.E curriculum, it is our aim that children skillfully and inquisitively develop their understanding of religions and worldviews. We encourage them to ask questions and enquire about the beliefs, values and traditions that belong to different communities and cultures around the world.
By promoting religious literacy, our curriculum enables children to use their knowledge and understanding, both from within school and the wider community, to engage in informed and balanced conversations about religions, beliefs and moral issues.
How we deliver our curriculum
We use the Diocese of Oxford’s scheme of learning ‘Living Faith’ and ‘Understanding Christianity’ scheme, alongside our own purposeful and relevant RE lessons to meet the needs and engagement of the children.
This enables a progression in knowledge and skills throughout the school. Lessons are designed to meet these aims, whilst engaging the class through various means such as stories, debates and visuals. The purpose of religious education does not include any attempt to alter a child’s beliefs.
How we support everyone to learn
We aim to make sure that all children are able to participate in RE lessons. Teachers have the flexibility to design their lessons and tasks to meet the needs and be considerate of the backgrounds and personal circumstances of the children in our classes. Suitable learning challenges are given to enable all children to engage and respond in what is being taught. To over come barriers to learning, children have a variety of provision such as the use of visuals, physical artefacts and writing tools to support purposeful and independent learning.
